questions.prompt: What is the average time complexity of searching for a key in a balanced binary search tree with n nodes?
questions.explanation: A balanced BST keeps its height at O(log n), and each comparison discards half the remaining subtree. An unbalanced tree degrades to O(n).

questions.prompt: Which data structure gives O(1) average insertion, deletion and lookup by key?
questions.explanation: With a good hash function and a bounded load factor, all three operations are O(1) expected. Worst case degrades to O(n) when every key collides.

questions.prompt: Which traversal visits graph nodes in order of increasing distance from the source?
questions.explanation: BFS explores level by level using a FIFO queue, which yields shortest paths on unweighted graphs. DFS gives no such guarantee.

questions.prompt: In dynamic programming, what distinguishes memoization from tabulation?

options.text: Memoization is top-down and lazy; tabulation is bottom-up and eager
Tabulation only works on tree-shaped problems

questions.explanation: Memoization recurses and caches subproblem results as they are needed, so it only computes reachable states. Tabulation fills a table iteratively from the base cases upward.

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of the standard 0/1 knapsack DP for n items and capacity W?
questions.explanation: The table has n rows and W columns and each cell is filled in constant time. This is pseudo-polynomial: W is a value, not an input length, so it is exponential in the bits of W.

questions.prompt: Which sorting algorithm has O(n log n) worst-case time AND sorts in place?
questions.explanation: Heapsort is both in-place and O(n log n) in the worst case. Quicksort degrades to O(n^2) in the worst case, and merge sort needs O(n) auxiliary space.

questions.prompt: You need the k largest elements from a stream of n numbers, where k is much smaller than n. What is the most space-efficient approach?

options.text: Sort the whole stream, then take the last k
Maintain a min-heap of size k
Maintain a max-heap of size n
Use a hash table keyed by value

questions.explanation: A size-k min-heap holds the best k seen so far in O(k) space; each new element is compared against the root and replaces it if larger. Total time is O(n log k).

questions.prompt: Which algorithm finds shortest paths from a single source on a graph that may contain negative edge weights?
questions.explanation: Bellman-Ford relaxes every edge V-1 times, tolerating negative weights and detecting negative cycles. Dijkstra assumes non-negative weights because it finalises nodes greedily.

questions.prompt: What is the amortised time complexity of appending to a dynamic array that doubles its capacity when full?
questions.explanation: Individual resizes cost O(n), but doubling means they happen geometrically rarely. The total cost of n appends is O(n), so each is O(1) amortised.

questions.prompt: Which technique is most appropriate for finding the longest substring without repeating characters in O(n)?

options.text: Sliding window with a hash set

questions.explanation: A window expands to the right and contracts from the left whenever a duplicate enters, so each character is visited at most twice — O(n) overall.
